title: Intake Medicals
goal: Every player has spoken in character, and every character has been told privately that their blood screen came back irregular and not to worry about it. By the end they know it happened to all six of them.
howToPlay: A school medical crossed with a passport office. Warm, slow, faintly ridiculous. Nobody is in danger here and nothing bad happens.

accomplishment.forWhat: Working out, without being told, that all six of them were flagged.

intro.where: The Directorate's medical hall on the combined campus, first morning of intake. Forty seventeen-year-olds in a queue that has not moved in eleven minutes.
intro.firstThing: A hand-lettered sign reading FORMS FIRST — NO EXCEPTIONS, taped over an older sign reading MEDICALS FIRST.
intro.readAloud:
There are forty of you and one queue, and it has not moved in eleven minutes. Somewhere ahead a man is saying "other arm" over and over in exactly the same tone.

A hand-lettered sign says FORMS FIRST — NO EXCEPTIONS. It is taped over an older sign, in better handwriting, that says MEDICALS FIRST.

carriesIn.when: This is the campaign's first scene
carriesIn.then: Nothing carries in. Everything here is a first impression, so give each player one unhurried moment to make one.

brief.wants: To get through forty medicals before lunch. That is genuinely all he wants, and he is very good at it.
brief.opensWith: "Name. Not the one on the form — the one you actually use."

willDiscuss.note: How many of these he has done. The number he gives is high and he is not exaggerating.
He processed them too, and remembers them. This is charming and should stay charming.
He will talk about anything except the flag, and he is good company.

willNotDiscuss.why: He is forbidden from saying. He also thinks the rule is stupid, and both facts show to anyone who reads him.

coercible.topic: A standing offer to come back to him later
coercible.how: Being liked. Pressure makes him bureaucratic rather than frightened — he has outlasted better interrogators than a seventeen-year-old.

voice.register: Brisk, warm, deadpan. Talks while doing something else. Never looks up.
tics: Compares them to relatives he processed decades ago
samples: "Arm. Other arm. Look at the light, not at me."
"You're the fourth Ishikawa I've had through here and none of you can sit still."
"It's a screen. Screens flag things. You're fine."
"Don't go home and worry your mother about it."

brief.wants: For the forms to be filled in correctly. She has no other ambitions today.
brief.opensWith: Which box they have got wrong.

willDiscuss.note: Box four goes to Records and box nineteen goes to Welfare, and the two departments have not spoken since the flood. She is not embarrassed by this.

voice.register: Flat, patient, entirely without irony. She has explained this many times and will explain it again.
tics: Answers the question she was asked and then stops talking
samples: "Box four is mother's maiden name. Box nineteen is also mother's maiden name, but in capitals."
"Records and Welfare haven't spoken since the flood."

beats.text: Go round the table once. Every player says one thing in character before anything else happens.
beats.direction: Do not make this a round of introductions. Give them something to react to — the queue not moving, the two contradictory signs, somebody else's terrible handwriting — and let them talk to each other rather than to you.
beats.note: This is the first time these six people have been in a room together. It is worth two minutes.

beats.text: Hand out Form 12-B. It asks for mother's maiden name in box 4, and again in box 19, in capitals.
beats.readAloud: "Box four is mother's maiden name. Box nineteen is also mother's maiden name, but in capitals. No, I don't know why. Box four goes to Records and box nineteen goes to Welfare, and Records and Welfare haven't spoken since the flood."
beats.direction: Play it for the laugh and do not explain it. This is a joke and it is also the entire Directorate in one piece of paper: two centuries of an institution that has never been tested and has never thrown anything away.

beats.text: Shucks sees them one at a time. Give each player about thirty seconds alone with him.
beats.direction: This is the only private moment in the session, and it is what makes the last beat land. If you can physically turn to one player and lower your voice, do that.

beats.text: Tell each of them privately that their screen came back irregular, that it is very common, and that they should not worry about it.
beats.readAloud: "Screen came back irregular. It does that. Half this queue will come back irregular. Don't go home and worry your mother about it."
beats.direction: Say it the same way six times. Bored, kind, already reaching for the next form. The flatness is what sells it.
beats.note: PLANT — mystery ledger #1, pays off Chapter 6. The screen is checking the city's children for traces of mitflit ancestry, because that is what lets a person link with a Frame's core. Nobody in the room knows this except Shucks, and he is not allowed to say it.

beats.text: They find out it happened to all six of them.
beats.direction: If a player raises it themselves, get out of the way and let the table run the scene. That is the best version and it usually happens on its own.
beats.note: IF NOBODY RAISES IT, three fallbacks in order of preference. (1) A kid from the queue who is not one of them says it loudly to nobody: "Did anyone else get irregular? My mum's going to lose it." (2) Shucks says it to the room on his way out: "That's the whole morning irregular. Records is going to have a lovely afternoon." (3) The clerk reads out the flagged list for collection. It is everyone, and she is not remotely bothered. Do not leave the scene without this planted.

beats.direction: He will not tell them and he is not being unkind about it. Deflect warmly, move them along, and let the deflection itself be the information.

when.condition: if anyone asks about the flag

beats.note: Every way at this is in data/challenges/c1s1-the-medical.json, each with its own DC and its own cost. If a player invents a different approach, price it on the scene's own ladder: DC 13 if it costs them something real, DC 15 for the obvious way, DC 17 if it is free or skips a step, DC 20 if it gets more than the scene was going to give them.

beats.text: Somebody gets a proper look at the paperwork.

when.condition: if a player goes for the form rather than the man

beats.note: On a success they keep it. This is the scene's artefact and the first thing in the campaign the party owns rather than was told.

artefacts.title: Form 12-B — Intake Screening (blank)
artefacts.earnedBy: Palming a copy of the form, or simply asking the clerk for a spare, which works and is funnier.
artefacts.gmNote: The tick-box marked IRREGULAR is PRE-PRINTED. Somebody expected this result often enough to have it typeset. That is the whole artefact — the party is meant to notice a printer's decision, not a conspiracy.
artefacts.body:
CITY CIVIL DEFENCE DIRECTORATE

Form 12-B — Intake Screening Record

4. Mother's maiden name  __________

5. Date of birth  ______

6. District of residence  __________

…

19. Mother's maiden name (CAPITALS)  __________

SCREENING RESULT — for completion by medical staff only

☐ Clear     ☐ Repeat     ☐ Irregular     ☐ Refer

Boxes 4 and 19 are collected separately. Do not amend one without amending the other.

Records copy — retain 40 years.

outro.endsWhen: The last of them is processed and the queue moves on to kit issue. If the all-six realisation has landed, end on it — do not play past it.
outro.readAloud: The queue shuffles forward. Somebody ahead is being told to look at the light and not at the doctor. Outside, it has started to rain on forty bicycles.

tracks.why: If the six of them worked the flag out together rather than being told, they have their first shared secret. That is what Bonds is for.
Only if somebody was caught going through the paperwork. Shucks finds it funny; Records does not. A small, survivable dent.

outro.onwards: Kit issue and ground role selection this afternoon, where Nobu signs the slips personally and is oddly generous with the allowance. Anyone who impressed Shucks this morning has a name he will remember.
writeDown: Which of the six worked out the pattern, and whether they told the others or kept it.
Who Shucks liked, and who he found funny. Both matter in Chapter 6.
Whether anyone treated the flag as frightening rather than annoying — that player is reading the campaign correctly and should be encouraged.

notes: First scene of the campaign. Its whole job is to make six strangers into a table and to plant one fact none of them can use yet. It contains no danger, no antagonist and no clock, and it should still be one of the sessions people remember, because it is the last time any of them are ordinary.
